papers.title: High-Dimensional Continuous Control Using Generalized Advantage Estimation
papers.authors: John Schulman, Philipp Moritz, Sergey Levine, Michael Jordan, Pieter Abbeel
papers.summary: 用指数加权的 TD 残差估计优势，通过 λ 控制偏差与方差。
papers.summary_en: Estimate advantages from exponentially weighted TD residuals, with lambda controlling the bias–variance tradeoff.
papers.scope: 实现 GAE 的反向递推和 episode 边界处理。
papers.scope_en: Implement the backward GAE recurrence and episode boundary handling.

papers.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms
papers.authors: John Schulman, Filip Wolski, Prafulla Dhariwal, Alec Radford, Oleg Klimov
papers.summary: 在策略目标中截断概率比，限制过大的策略更新带来的收益。
papers.summary_en: Clip probability ratios in the policy objective to limit the incentive for excessively large updates.
papers.scope: 实现 clipped surrogate 及其梯度行为；价值损失、归一化和统计代码已提供。
papers.scope_en: Implement the clipped surrogate and its gradient behavior; value loss, normalization, and diagnostics are supplied.

papers.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
papers.authors: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma, Eric Mitchell, Stefano Ermon, Christopher D. Manning, Chelsea Finn
papers.summary: 将偏好对上的隐式奖励差转化为直接优化语言模型的分类目标。
papers.summary_en: Turn the implicit reward margin of preference pairs into an objective that directly optimizes a language model.
papers.scope: 实现偏好损失与隐式奖励；token 对齐和序列 log-prob 计算已提供。
papers.scope_en: Implement the preference loss and implicit rewards; token alignment and sequence log-probability calculation are supplied.

papers.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
papers.authors: Zhihong Shao, Peiyi Wang, Qihao Zhu, Runxin Xu, Junxiao Song, Xiao Bi, Haowei Zhang, Mingchuan Zhang, Y. K. Li, Y. Wu, Daya Guo
papers.summary: 使用同一问题的一组回答构造相对优势，并通过 GRPO 目标更新策略。
papers.summary_en: Construct relative advantages from a group of responses to the same prompt and update the policy with the GRPO objective.
papers.scope: 选取论文的 GRPO 模块：组内相对优势、截断目标和回答级聚合。
papers.scope_en: Focus on the paper's GRPO module: group-relative advantages, clipped objectives, and response-level aggregation.

papers.title: Understanding R1-Zero-Like Training: A Critical Perspective
papers.authors: Zichen Liu, Changyu Chen, Wenjun Li, Penghui Qi, Tianyu Pang, Chao Du, Wee Sun Lee, Min Lin
papers.summary: 分析 GRPO 的长度与难度偏差，并调整优势缩放和损失归一化。
papers.summary_en: Analyze length and difficulty biases in GRPO and adjust advantage scaling and loss normalization.
papers.scope: 实现去除组内标准差缩放与固定生成长度归一化这两处修正。
papers.scope_en: Implement two corrections: remove group standard-deviation scaling and normalize by a fixed generation budget.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
papers.authors: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, Pieter Abbeel
papers.summary: 用逐步加噪的前向过程和学习去噪的反向过程构造生成模型。
papers.summary_en: Build a generative model from a forward noising process and a learned reverse denoising process.
papers.scope: 实现闭式前向加噪，以及高斯后验和 epsilon 参数化的反向一步；调度器与采样循环已提供。
papers.scope_en: Implement closed-form forward noising, the Gaussian posterior, and an epsilon-parameterized reverse step; schedules and sampling loops are supplied.

papers.title: Progressive Distillation for Fast Sampling of Diffusion Models
papers.summary: 把教师的两步确定性更新蒸馏为学生的一步更新，逐轮减少采样步数。
papers.summary_en: Distill two deterministic teacher steps into one student step, progressively reducing the sampling budget.
papers.scope: 先实现 v 参数化转换，再推导两步教师到一步学生的蒸馏目标并验证更新。
papers.scope_en: Implement v-parameterization conversions, then derive and validate the two-teacher-step to one-student-step distillation target.

papers.title: Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models
papers.authors: Jiaming Song, Chenlin Meng, Stefano Ermon
papers.summary: 使用非马尔可夫采样更新实现跳步生成，并以 eta 控制随机性。
papers.summary_en: Use a non-Markovian sampling update to skip timesteps, with eta controlling stochasticity.
papers.scope: 实现 DDIM 单步更新和干净端点；时间步选择、循环与反演探索代码已提供。
papers.scope_en: Implement the DDIM update and clean endpoint; timestep selection, loops, and inversion exploration code are supplied.

papers.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
papers.authors: Yaron Lipman, Ricky T. Q. Chen, Heli Ben-Hamu, Maximilian Nickel, Matt Le
papers.summary: 通过回归条件概率路径的速度场学习连续生成流。
papers.summary_en: Learn a continuous generative flow by regressing the velocity field of conditional probability paths.
papers.scope: 实现条件路径、目标速度和 CFM 回归损失；时间采样、Euler 积分和训练辅助代码已提供。
papers.scope_en: Implement the conditional path, target velocity, and CFM regression loss; time sampling, Euler integration, and training helpers are supplied.

papers.title: Group Sequence Policy Optimization
papers.summary: 在回答级别构造长度归一化的重要性比率，再截断策略目标。
papers.summary_en: Construct length-normalized sequence importance ratios and clip the policy objective at the response level.
papers.scope: 实现序列概率比与 GSPO 损失，验证掩码、截断区域和梯度。
papers.scope_en: Implement sequence ratios and the GSPO loss; test masking, clipping regions, and gradients.

papers.title: On-policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes
papers.summary: 在学生自己生成的前缀上查询教师分布，减少训练与生成时的分布偏移。
papers.summary_en: Query the teacher on student-generated prefixes to reduce the mismatch between training and generation.
papers.scope: 实现学生 rollout 和全词表散度；在小型自回归模型上验证。OPD 在此指 on-policy distillation。
papers.scope_en: Implement student rollouts and full-vocabulary divergence in a tiny autoregressive model. OPD here means on-policy distillation.

papers.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
papers.summary: 通过动态保留有效回答组、非对称截断和 token 级聚合改进策略优化。
papers.summary_en: Improve policy optimization with informative-group filtering, asymmetric clipping, and token-level aggregation.
papers.scope: 实现组筛选与 token 级目标；采样系统和分布式训练不在本模块范围。
papers.scope_en: Implement group filtering and the token-level objective; sampling infrastructure and distributed training are outside this module.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
papers.summary: 冻结预训练权重，以低秩矩阵乘积学习增量。
papers.summary_en: Freeze pretrained weights and learn an update through a low-rank matrix product.
papers.scope: 实现低秩增量和线性前向，验证冻结边界及小型回归学习。
papers.scope_en: Implement the low-rank update and linear forward pass; verify frozen parameters and a small regression experiment.

papers.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
papers.authors: Tim Dettmers, Artidoro Pagnoni, Ari Holtzman, Luke Zettlemoyer
papers.summary: 在量化的冻结基座上训练低秩适配器，以减少微调内存。
papers.summary_en: Train low-rank adapters on a quantized frozen base to reduce fine-tuning memory.
papers.scope: 实现分块 NF4 量化、反量化与适配器前向；不模拟双重量化或分页优化器。
papers.scope_en: Implement blockwise NF4 quantization, dequantization, and adapter forward; double quantization and paged optimizers are outside this exercise.

papers.title: Mean Flows for One-step Generative Modeling
papers.authors: Zhengyang Geng, Mingyang Deng, Xingjian Bai, J. Zico Kolter, Kaiming He
papers.summary: 用瞬时速度和平均速度之间的恒等式学习区间流，以一步生成样本。
papers.summary_en: Learn an interval flow using the identity between instantaneous and average velocities for one-step generation.
papers.scope: 实现平均流的 JVP 目标和梯度边界，并运行小型生成实验。
papers.scope_en: Implement the average-flow JVP target and gradient boundaries, then run a small generative experiment.

papers.title: Back to Basics: Let Denoising Generative Models Denoise
papers.summary: 直接预测干净数据，在不同预测空间和损失空间之间显式转换。
papers.summary_en: Predict clean data directly and explicitly convert between prediction and loss spaces.
papers.scope: 实现 x-prediction 到速度的转换与去噪目标，使用论文启发的低维流形嵌入实验。
papers.scope_en: Implement data-to-velocity conversion and the denoising objective with a paper-derived embedded-manifold experiment.

papers.title: Generative Modeling via Drifting
papers.authors: Mingyang Deng, He Li, Tianhong Li, Yilun Du, Kaiming He
papers.summary: 构造吸引真实样本、排斥生成样本的漂移场，并用停止梯度的目标训练生成器。
papers.summary_en: Construct a drifting field that attracts real samples and repels generated samples, then train a generator against a stopped-gradient target.
papers.scope: 实现漂移场与停止梯度损失，在小型二维分布上验证生成器行为。
papers.scope_en: Implement the drifting field and stopped-gradient loss, and verify generator behavior on a small two-dimensional distribution.

papers.title: One-step Diffusion with Distribution Matching Distillation
papers.authors: Tianwei Yin, Michaël Gharbi, Richard Zhang, Eli Shechtman, Fredo Durand, William T. Freeman, Taesung Park
papers.summary: 用真实分布和生成分布的 score 差构造生成器的分布匹配更新。
papers.summary_en: Use the score difference between real and generated distributions to construct a distribution-matching generator update.
papers.scope: 实现 score 差目标与配对回归项，用解析双峰分布检查模式覆盖。
papers.scope_en: Implement the score-difference target and paired regression term; inspect mode coverage using an analytic bimodal distribution.

papers.title: Improved Distribution Matching Distillation for Fast Image Synthesis
papers.authors: Tianwei Yin, Michaël Gharbi, Taesung Park, Richard Zhang, Eli Shechtman, Fredo Durand, William T. Freeman
papers.summary: 通过更快的假 score 更新和对抗辅助训练，去除 DMD 的配对回归要求。
papers.summary_en: Remove DMD's paired-regression requirement using faster fake-score updates and adversarial auxiliary training.
papers.scope: 实现双时间尺度更新与辅助目标，在小型实验中验证参数更新边界。
papers.scope_en: Implement two-timescale updates and auxiliary objectives; verify parameter-update boundaries in a small experiment.

papers.title: Consistency Models
papers.authors: Yang Song, Prafulla Dhariwal, Mark Chen, Ilya Sutskever
papers.summary: 让同一生成轨迹上的不同噪声状态映射到一致的干净端点。
papers.summary_en: Map noisy states along the same generative trajectory to a consistent clean endpoint.
papers.scope: 实现边界参数化和相邻时刻的一致性蒸馏损失。
papers.scope_en: Implement the boundary parameterization and adjacent-time consistency-distillation loss.

papers.title: Attention Is All You Need
papers.summary: 用多头注意力组合序列信息，结合位置编码、逐位置前馈网络和残差归一化构成 Transformer。
papers.summary_en: Combine sequence information through multi-head attention, positional encoding, position-wise feed-forward networks, and residual normalization.
papers.scope: 分别实现缩放点积注意力、多头注意力、LayerNorm 与 Add & Norm、正弦位置编码及逐位置前馈网络；每个模块独立练习，辅助代码与小实验已提供。
papers.scope_en: Independently implement scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, LayerNorm and Add & Norm, sinusoidal positional encoding, and position-wise feed-forward networks; helpers and small experiments are supplied.

papers.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
papers.summary: 将权重衰减与自适应梯度更新分离。
papers.summary_en: Decouple weight decay from the adaptive gradient update.
papers.scope: 实现矩估计、偏差修正与解耦权重衰减的一步更新。
papers.scope_en: Implement moment estimates, bias correction, and a decoupled weight-decay step.

papers.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
papers.authors: Tri Dao, Daniel Y. Fu, Stefano Ermon, Atri Rudra, Christopher Ré
papers.summary: 利用在线 softmax 分块精确累积注意力，避免物化完整注意力矩阵。
papers.summary_en: Accumulate exact attention in blocks with online softmax without materializing the full attention matrix.
papers.scope: 实现分块递推与重缩放。这是 CPU 算法练习，不评价 GPU kernel 性能。
papers.scope_en: Implement blockwise recurrence and rescaling. This CPU algorithm exercise does not benchmark GPU kernels.

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.summary: 用对称的批内对比损失对齐图像和文本表征。
papers.summary_en: Align image and text representations using a symmetric in-batch contrastive objective.
papers.scope: 实现特征归一化、温度缩放和双向对比损失，使用小型配对检索实验。
papers.scope_en: Implement feature normalization, temperature scaling, and bidirectional contrastive loss with a tiny paired-retrieval experiment.

papers.title: GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering
papers.summary: 从 GLM-5 技术报告中提取按注意力头正交化的优化更新，以及异步强化学习的重要性采样修正。
papers.summary_en: Extract head-wise orthogonalized updates and asynchronous-RL importance corrections from the GLM-5 technical report.
papers.scope: 两题分别实现 Muon Split 的逐头正交化与双边重要性采样策略损失，使用可复现的 CPU 教学实验。
papers.scope_en: Implement Muon Split's per-head orthogonalization and a double-sided importance-sampling policy loss in two independent CPU exercises.

papers.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
papers.summary: 实现 Kimi K3 在序列、深度和激活值三个维度的核心机制：KDA、块级注意力残差与 SiTU-GLU。
papers.summary_en: Implement Kimi K3's core mechanisms for sequence mixing, depth aggregation, and bounded activations: KDA, Block AttnRes, and SiTU-GLU.
papers.scope: 三题分别实现有界衰减与 delta-rule 递推、跨层残差注意力聚合、SiTU 门控激活，并重绘论文中的门函数与激活曲线。
papers.scope_en: Independently implement bounded decay and delta-rule recurrence, attention over residual blocks, and SiTU gating; recreate the report's decay and activation curves.

papers.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.summary: 用同一模型的特权上下文教师监督学生自己的轨迹。
papers.summary_en: Use a privileged-context teacher from the same model to supervise student rollouts.
papers.scope: 双上下文因果对齐与逐词表项散度截断。
papers.scope_en: Dual-context causal alignment and pointwise divergence clipping.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning via Self-Distillation
papers.summary: 将环境反馈与成功尝试转成逐 token 的自蒸馏监督。
papers.summary_en: Turn environment feedback and successful attempts into token-level self-distillation.
papers.scope: 同题反馈路由、reverse KL 与 top-k 尾部概率聚合。
papers.scope_en: Same-question feedback routing, reverse KL, and top-k tail-mass coarsening.

papers.title: Representation Alignment for Generation: Training Diffusion Transformers Is Easier Than You Think
papers.summary: 将生成模型的中间特征与冻结教师的语义表征对齐。
papers.summary_en: Align intermediate generative features with a frozen semantic teacher.
papers.scope: 逐 patch 表征对齐损失与梯度边界。
papers.scope_en: Patch-wise representation alignment and gradient boundaries.

papers.title: Restructuring Vector Quantization with the Rotation Trick
papers.summary: 以冻结旋转与缩放构造向量量化的代理梯度。
papers.summary_en: Use a frozen rotation and scale to construct vector-quantization surrogate gradients.
papers.scope: 保持量化前向值的旋转梯度变换。
papers.scope_en: Rotation-based gradient transformation with quantized forward values.

papers.title: Differential Transformer
papers.summary: 相减两张注意力图以抑制共有噪声。
papers.summary_en: Subtract two attention maps to suppress common-mode noise.
papers.scope: 已投影张量上的差分注意力与 lambda 参数化。
papers.scope_en: Differential attention on projected tensors and lambda parameterization.

papers.title: Block Diffusion: Interpolating Between Autoregressive and Diffusion Language Models
papers.summary: 以块间自回归和块内扩散结合离散生成。
papers.summary_en: Combine autoregression across blocks with diffusion within blocks.
papers.scope: 拼接干净和含噪 token 的单次前向注意力掩码。
papers.scope_en: Single-forward attention masks for concatenated noisy and clean tokens.

papers.title: DistiLLM-2: A Contrastive Approach Boosts the Distillation of LLMs
papers.summary: 在教师与学生生成的数据上分别使用不同的蒸馏方向。
papers.summary_en: Use distinct distillation directions on teacher- and student-generated responses.
papers.scope: 教师轨迹的 skew KL 与学生轨迹的 skew reverse KL。
papers.scope_en: Skew KL on teacher trajectories and skew reverse KL on student trajectories.

papers.title: Pass@K Policy Optimization: Solving Harder Reinforcement Learning Problems
papers.summary: 将 pass@k 目标的奖励变换用于策略梯度训练。
papers.summary_en: Transform rewards to optimize a pass@k policy-gradient objective.
papers.scope: 连续奖励变换、policy loss 与论文的一维 Gaussian toy。
papers.scope_en: Continuous-reward transformation, policy loss, and the paper’s one-dimensional Gaussian toy.

papers.title: SVDQuant: Absorbing Outliers by Low-Rank Components for 4-Bit Diffusion Models
papers.summary: 用高精度低秩支路吸收量化困难成分，再量化残差。
papers.summary_en: Absorb difficult-to-quantize components in a high-precision low-rank branch and quantize the residual.
papers.scope: 平滑、SVD 低秩分解与 4-bit 残差前向。
papers.scope_en: Smoothing, SVD low-rank decomposition, and a 4-bit residual forward pass.

papers.title: MoGe: Unlocking Accurate Monocular Geometry Estimation for Open-Domain Images with Optimal Training Supervision
papers.summary: 通过鲁棒几何对齐处理单目预测中的尺度与深度偏移。
papers.summary_en: Use robust geometric alignment to handle scale and depth-shift ambiguity in monocular predictions.
papers.scope: 截断加权 L1 的鲁棒最优估计。
papers.scope_en: Robust optimal estimation with truncated weighted L1 residuals.

papers.title: Improving Diffusion Inverse Problem Solving with Decoupled Noise Annealing
papers.summary: 将干净空间的测量一致性优化与重新加噪解耦。
papers.summary_en: Decouple measurement-consistency updates in clean space from renoising.
papers.scope: 线性 Gaussian 后验 score、Langevin 与独立重新加噪。
papers.scope_en: Linear-Gaussian posterior score, Langevin updates, and independent renoising.

papers.title: DiffusionNFT: Online Diffusion Reinforcement with Forward Process
papers.summary: 从反馈构造正负隐式速度场，优化扩散模型。
papers.summary_en: Construct positive and negative implicit velocity fields from feedback to optimize diffusion models.
papers.scope: 正负 beta 隐式速度、双分支目标与微型训练。
papers.scope_en: Positive/negative beta implicit velocities, the two-branch objective, and tiny training.

papers.title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
papers.summary: 按从粗到细的尺度顺序生成视觉 token，并在同一尺度内并行预测。
papers.summary_en: Generate visual tokens from coarse to fine, predicting tokens within each scale in parallel.
papers.scope: 下一尺度的条件输入与注意力掩码，以及多尺度残差量化与重建。
papers.scope_en: Next-scale conditioning and attention masks, plus multiscale residual quantization and reconstruction.

papers.title: Representation Fréchet Loss for Visual Generation
papers.authors: Jiawei Yang, Zhengyang Geng, Xuan Ju, Yonglong Tian, Yue Wang
papers.summary: 以历史特征统计估计更大的样本总体，只对当前 batch 反传 Fréchet 距离。
papers.summary_en: Estimate a larger feature population from historical statistics while backpropagating Fréchet distance through the current batch only.
papers.scope: 原始一阶与二阶矩的 EMA、协方差恢复、可微 Fréchet 距离和多表征损失归一化。
papers.scope_en: EMA of raw first and second moments, covariance recovery, differentiable Fréchet distance, and multi-representation loss normalization.

papers.title: VICReg: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning
papers.authors: Adrien Bardes, Jean Ponce, Yann LeCun
papers.summary: 用方差、视图一致性与去相关约束学习表征。
papers.summary_en: Learn representations with variance, view invariance, and decorrelation constraints.
papers.scope: 三项损失的批统计、权重与梯度。
papers.scope_en: Batch statistics, weights, and gradients of the three loss terms.

papers.title: LeJEPA: Provable and Scalable Self-Supervised Learning Without the Heuristics
papers.summary: 用随机投影上的高斯性约束学习各向同性表征。
papers.summary_en: Learn isotropic representations with Gaussianity constraints on random projections.
papers.scope: SIGReg 的特征函数检验、数值积分与切片聚合。
papers.scope_en: SIGReg characteristic-function statistics, numerical integration, and slice aggregation.

papers.title: VISReg: Variance-Invariance-Sketching Regularization for JEPA training
papers.authors: Haiyu Wu, Randall Balestriero, Morgan Levine
papers.summary: 分离表征的尺度与分布形状，用切片匹配约束高斯性。
papers.summary_en: Separate representation scale and distribution shape with sliced Gaussian matching.
papers.scope: 尺度、切片形状、中心与多视图一致性损失。
papers.scope_en: Scale, sliced shape, centering, and multi-view invariance losses.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning from Images with a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture
papers.authors: Mahmoud Assran, Quentin Duval, Ishan Misra, Piotr Bojanowski, Pascal Vincent, Michael Rabbat, Yann LeCun, Nicolas Ballas
papers.summary: 从上下文预测被遮挡图像块的教师表征。
papers.summary_en: Predict teacher representations of masked image blocks from context.
papers.scope: 目标块提取、预测损失与 EMA 教师更新。
papers.scope_en: Target-block gathering, prediction loss, and EMA teacher updates.

papers.title: LeWorldModel: Stable End-to-End Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture from Pixels
papers.authors: Lucas Maes, Quentin Le Lidec, Damien Scieur, Yann LeCun, Randall Balestriero
papers.summary: 联合学习动作条件潜空间预测，并用潜空间 rollout 规划动作。
papers.summary_en: Jointly learn action-conditioned latent predictions and plan actions with latent rollouts.
papers.scope: 可微预测与正则目标、自回归 rollout、终点代价和 CEM 精英重拟合。
papers.scope_en: Differentiable prediction and regularization, autoregressive rollout, terminal cost, and CEM elite refitting.

papers.title: Causal-JEPA: Learning World Models through Object-Level Latent Masking
papers.authors: Heejeong Nam, Quentin Le Lidec, Lucas Maes, Yann LeCun, Randall Balestriero
papers.summary: 遮挡对象的潜空间轨迹，让模型从其他对象推断其动态。
papers.summary_en: Mask object-level latent trajectories to infer their dynamics from other objects.
papers.scope: 保留初始身份锚点的对象遮挡与历史、未来预测损失。
papers.scope_en: Object masking with initial identity anchors and history/future prediction losses.

papers.title: Root Mean Square Layer Normalization
papers.summary: 用均方根代替去均值的归一化，并研究部分特征统计。
papers.summary_en: Normalize by root mean square without centering and explore partial feature statistics.

problems.starter:
import torch
from torch import Tensor


# Required: implement the core functions below.
def clipped_surrogate(new_logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, advantages: Tensor,
                      clip_eps: float = 0.2) -> Tensor:
    """Minimized PPO policy loss for [B] log-probs and already prepared advantages.

    Freeze the old policy and advantages; keep gradients through new_logp. Return one
    scalar. Advantage normalization is supplied by ppo_loss.

    Returns:
        Return one floating scalar Tensor loss, shape (): the negative batch mean of the
        clipped policy surrogate for [B] inputs. Preserve input floating dtype/device.
        Retain gradients through new_logp; freeze old_logp and advantages. Return the Tensor
        itself, without .item() or .detach().
    """
    raise NotImplementedError()


# Provided: keep these helpers and call them as needed.
def ppo_loss(new_logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, advantages: Tensor, new_values: Tensor,
             old_values: Tensor, returns: Tensor, entropy: Tensor | None = None,
             clip_eps: float = 0.2, vf_clip: float | None = 0.2, vf_coef: float = 0.5,
             ent_coef: float = 0.0, norm_adv: bool = True) -> dict[str, Tensor]:
    """Provided training adapter: normalization, value/entropy terms, diagnostics.

    Returns:
        dict[str, Tensor] with scalar () values: loss (total objective), pg_loss, v_loss
        (half mean value error), entropy (mean or zero), approx_kl and clipfrac. Only
        approx_kl/clipfrac are detached diagnostics. Current policy/value loss paths stay
        live; old policy/values and advantage/return targets are frozen.
    """
    old_values = old_values.detach()
    advantages, returns = advantages.detach(), returns.detach()
    if norm_adv:
        std = advantages.std(unbiased=True) if advantages.numel() > 1 else advantages.new_zeros(())
        advantages = (advantages - advantages.mean()) / (std + 1e-8)
    pg_loss = clipped_surrogate(new_logp, old_logp, advantages, clip_eps)
    value_error = (new_values - returns).square()
    if vf_clip is not None:
        v_clipped = old_values + (new_values - old_values).clamp(-vf_clip, vf_clip)
        value_error = torch.maximum(value_error, (v_clipped - returns).square())
    v_loss = 0.5 * value_error.mean()
    ent = new_logp.new_zeros(()) if entropy is None else entropy.mean()
    with torch.no_grad():
        logratio = new_logp - old_logp.detach()
        ratio = logratio.exp()
        approx_kl = (ratio - 1 - logratio).mean()
        clipfrac = ((ratio - 1).abs() > clip_eps).to(new_logp.dtype).mean()
    return dict(loss=pg_loss + vf_coef * v_loss - ent_coef * ent, pg_loss=pg_loss,
                v_loss=v_loss, entropy=ent, approx_kl=approx_kl, clipfrac=clipfrac)

    """Four [B] sequence log-probs; label_smoothing weights reversed labels.

        batch mean, retaining policy gradients (no item/detach). chosen_rewards: beta *

def sequence_logprob(logits: Tensor, input_ids: Tensor, loss_mask: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Provided helper: shift labels/mask and sum response log-probabilities.

    Returns:
        Returns one floating Tensor scores, shape [B], from logits [B, T, V] (T positions, V
        vocabulary entries). Each value is the sum of shifted, masked response-token
        log-probabilities, not a token mean. Preserve logits dtype/device and gradients; B=1

    scores = logits[:, :-1].log_softmax(-1)
    selected = scores.gather(-1, input_ids[:, 1:].unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
    return (selected * loss_mask[:, 1:]).sum(-1)

import torch
from torch import Tensor


# Required: implement the core functions below.
def grpo_advantages(rewards: Tensor, group_size: int, scale_std: bool=True, eps: float=0.0001) -> Tensor:
    """rewards [B*G] contains adjacent groups of G answers to each prompt. Use sample std
    (correction=1) plus eps when scale_std=True. Return [B*G]; G must be >=2 and divide the
    reward count.

    Returns:
        Return one floating Tensor advantages, shape [B * G], in the original adjacent-group
        order (B prompts, G = group_size responses each). Preserve rewards dtype/device.
        Center within each group; divide by sample std plus eps only when scale_std=True. Do
        not return a [B, G] matrix or a scalar reduction.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError()

def grpo_loss(logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, ref_logp: Tensor, advantages: Tensor, mask: Tensor, clip_eps: float=0.2, beta: float=0.04) -> tuple[Tensor, dict]:
    """logp/old_logp/ref_logp and binary mask are [N,L]; advantages [N]. Freeze old/ref
    snapshots. Average effective tokens within each response, then average responses. Empty
    responses contribute zero. Return scalar loss and detached kl_mean, clipfrac,
    ratio_mean, averaged over valid tokens. clipfrac counts abs(ratio-1)>clip_eps.

    Returns:
        (loss, stats): scalar Tensor () and dict of scalar Tensors. loss averages valid
        tokens per response, then all responses (empty = zero). stats keys: kl_mean,
        clipfrac, ratio_mean; detached valid-token means, all zero for an empty mask. loss
        keeps logp gradients; old/ref/advantages frozen.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError()


# Provided: keep these helpers and call them as needed.
def masked_logprobs(logp: Tensor, old_logp: Tensor, ref_logp: Tensor, mask: Tensor):
    """Provided helper: neutralize padding before exponential calculations.

    Returns:
        Returns (masked_logp, masked_old_logp, masked_ref_logp) in the same order as the
        three score inputs. Each Tensor keeps its input's [N, L] shape, dtype and device,
        with zero at masked positions and unchanged scores elsewhere. This helper preserves
        active-position gradient paths; the loss caller freezes old/reference scores
        separately.
    """
    active = mask.bool()
    return tuple(torch.where(active, x, torch.zeros_like(x)) for x in (logp, old_logp, ref_logp))

def token_statistics(ratio: Tensor, kl: Tensor, mask: Tensor, clip_eps: float) -> dict:
    """Provided helper: detached diagnostics averaged over valid tokens.

    Returns:
        dict[str, Tensor]: kl_mean, clipfrac, ratio_mean, each scalar (). All are detached
        valid-token means, or zero when no tokens are valid. clipfrac counts abs(ratio - 1)
        > clip_eps.
    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        denom = mask.sum().clamp_min(1)
        return dict(kl_mean=(kl * mask).sum() / denom,
                    clipfrac=(((ratio - 1).abs() > clip_eps) * mask).sum() / denom,
                    ratio_mean=(ratio * mask).sum() / denom)

import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor


# Core implementation
def q_sample(x0: Tensor, t: Tensor, noise: Tensor, alpha_bars: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """x0/noise [B,...], t [B] long; return x0's shape and dtype.

    Returns:
        Return the noisy Tensor at each sample time, matching x0 shape [B,...] and
        dtype/device; B is batch size and trailing axes are arbitrary sample dimensions.
        Selected alpha_bars coefficients must use x0 dtype/device, rather than promoting
        float32 samples to float64. Return only samples, preserve differentiable paths, and
        leave inputs unchanged.
    """
    # TODO: implement the selected core module.
    raise NotImplementedError


# Provided helpers
def linear_betas(T: int, beta_start: float = 1e-4, beta_end: float = 0.02) -> Tensor:
    """Return [T] float64 linearly spaced variances.

    Returns:
        Return a torch.float64 Tensor of shape [T] (CPU by default here), containing one
        noise variance beta per level. Indices 0..T-1 correspond to paper times 1..T. For
        T>=2, include both beta_start and beta_end; for T=1, the only value is beta_start.
        This is not cumulative alpha or a Python list. The output is gradient-free.
    """
    return torch.linspace(beta_start, beta_end, T, dtype=torch.float64)

def cosine_betas(T: int, s: float = 0.008, max_beta: float = 0.999) -> Tensor:
    """Discretize cosine cumulative alpha and clip beta.

    Returns:
        Return a torch.float64 Tensor of shape [T] (CPU by default here), containing
        per-step betas from the discretized cosine schedule, bounded above by max_beta.
        Return T entries, not T+1 or cumulative alpha. The output is gradient-free.
    """
    time = torch.linspace(0, 1, T + 1, dtype=torch.float64)
    f = torch.cos((time + s) / (1 + s) * math.pi / 2).square()
    return (1 - f[1:] / f[:-1]).clamp(max=max_beta)

def make_schedule(betas: Tensor) -> dict[str, Tensor]:
    """All values [T] float64; alpha_bars_prev[0] = 1.

    Returns:
        Return a dict[str, Tensor] with exactly these six keys: alphas, alpha_bars,
        alpha_bars_prev, sqrt_alpha_bars, sqrt_one_minus_alpha_bars, log_snr. Every value
        has shape [T], torch.float64 dtype and betas device, where T=len(betas);
        alpha_bars_prev starts at 1. There is no betas key and no tuple return. Keep
        differentiable computation and leave betas unchanged.
    """
    alphas = 1 - betas.double()
    ab = alphas.cumprod(0)
    prev = torch.cat((torch.ones_like(ab[:1]), ab[:-1]))
    return {"alphas": alphas, "alpha_bars": ab, "alpha_bars_prev": prev,
            "sqrt_alpha_bars": ab.sqrt(), "sqrt_one_minus_alpha_bars": (1 - ab).sqrt(),
            "log_snr": ab.log() - torch.log1p(-ab)}

def v_to_eps(x_t: Tensor, v: Tensor, alpha: Tensor, sigma: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Inverse orthogonal rotation, stable at both endpoints.

    Returns:
        Return one Tensor of noise recovered from v, matching x_t shape [B,...]; B is batch
        size and trailing axes are sample coordinates. alpha/sigma are already broadcastable
        by the input convention; do not add coefficient axes. Preserve the documented
        matching floating dtype/device and gradients. Do not return multiple
        parameterizations as a tuple or mutate inputs.
    """

    raise NotImplementedError


# Provided helpers
def eps_to_x0(x_t: Tensor, eps: Tensor, alpha: Tensor, sigma: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Recover clean data; coefficients broadcast to x_t, denominator >= 1e-8.

    Returns:
        Return one Tensor of clean data recovered from a noise prediction, matching x_t
        shape [B,...]; B is batch size and trailing axes are sample coordinates. alpha/sigma
        are already broadcastable by the input convention; do not add coefficient axes.
        Preserve the documented matching floating dtype/device and gradients. Do not return
        multiple parameterizations as a tuple or mutate inputs.
    """
    return (x_t - sigma * eps) / alpha.clamp(min=1e-8)

def x0_to_eps(x_t: Tensor, x0: Tensor, alpha: Tensor, sigma: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Recover noise, retaining finite values at the clean endpoint.

    Returns:
        Return one Tensor of noise recovered from a clean-data prediction, matching x_t
        shape [B,...]; B is batch size and trailing axes are sample coordinates. alpha/sigma
        are already broadcastable by the input convention; do not add coefficient axes.
        Preserve the documented matching floating dtype/device and gradients. Do not return
        multiple parameterizations as a tuple or mutate inputs.
    """
    return (x_t - alpha * x0) / sigma.clamp(min=1e-8)

def convert(pred: Tensor, src: str, dst: str, x_t: Tensor, alpha: Tensor, sigma: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Convert a prediction between x0, eps and v; preserve shape/dtype.

    Returns:
        Return one Tensor in the dst parameterization, with pred/x_t shape [B,...],
        preserving the documented matching floating dtype/device and gradients. When
        src=dst, return pred directly (the same object); otherwise return the converted
        prediction. Do not return a dictionary of x0/eps/v or mutate inputs.
    """
    if src not in {"x0", "eps", "v"} or dst not in {"x0", "eps", "v"}:
        raise ValueError("src and dst must be x0, eps or v")
    if src == dst:
        return pred
    if src == "v":
        return v_to_x0(x_t, pred, alpha, sigma) if dst == "x0" else v_to_eps(x_t, pred, alpha, sigma)
    x0 = pred if src == "x0" else eps_to_x0(x_t, pred, alpha, sigma)
    eps = pred if src == "eps" else x0_to_eps(x_t, pred, alpha, sigma)
    return {"x0": x0, "eps": eps, "v": make_v(x0, eps, alpha, sigma)}[dst]

        differentiable paths through values. Leave all inputs unchanged.

def ddpm_sample(eps_model: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor], shape: tuple[int, ...], betas: Tensor, generator: torch.Generator, var_type: str = "posterior", return_traj: bool = False) -> Tensor | tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:

        returned tensors are gradient-free.

        if return_traj:
            trajectory.append(x.clone())
    return (x, torch.stack(trajectory)) if return_traj else x

"""Implement only the TODO functions; supporting routines are provided.

Required: ddim_step.
Provided: ddim_timesteps, ddim_sample, ddim_invert.
"""
import torch
from torch import Tensor
from typing import Callable


# Core implementation
def ddim_step(x_t: Tensor, eps_pred: Tensor, ab_t: Tensor, ab_prev: Tensor,
              eta: float, noise: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Coefficients broadcast to x_t; final ab_prev=1.

    Returns:
        Return the sample Tensor at the less noisy destination, matching x_t shape [B,...]
        and floating dtype/device; B is batch size and trailing axes are sample dimensions.
        Do not return the clean prediction or coefficients. eta=0 removes dependence on
        noise; ab_prev=1 returns the clean endpoint. This step does not itself stop
        gradients.
    """
    # TODO: implement the selected core module.
    raise NotImplementedError


# Provided helpers
def ddim_timesteps(T: int, num_steps: int) -> Tensor:
    """[num_steps] long: T-1-k*(T//num_steps), strict descending.

    Returns:
        Return a torch.long Tensor of shape [num_steps] (CPU by default here), containing
        strictly descending discrete indices starting at T-1. Each entry corresponds to one
        model call. The final clean boundary is not an extra entry, and index 0 need not
        occur. The output has no gradients.
    """
    if not 1 <= num_steps <= T:
        raise ValueError("num_steps must lie in [1,T]")
    return T - 1 - torch.arange(num_steps, dtype=torch.long) * (T // num_steps)

@torch.no_grad()
def ddim_sample(eps_model: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor], x_T: Tensor, alpha_bars: Tensor, num_steps: int, eta: float = 0.0, generator: torch.Generator | None = None, return_traj: bool = False) -> Tensor | tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Return samples or (samples, trajectory including x_T and clean endpoint).

    Returns:
        With return_traj=False, return final samples as a Tensor [B,...], matching x_T shape
        and dtype/device. With True, return the tuple (samples, trajectory) in that order.
        trajectory is a Tensor [num_steps+1,B,...]: entry 0 copies x_T, each following entry
        is one update, and the last equals samples. Both outputs are gradient-free; x_T is
        unchanged.
    """
    steps = ddim_timesteps(len(alpha_bars), num_steps).tolist()
    ab = alpha_bars.to(x_T)
    x = x_T.clone()
    trajectory = [x.clone()] if return_traj else None
    for i, step in enumerate(steps):
        previous = ab[steps[i + 1]] if i + 1 < len(steps) else torch.ones_like(ab[0])
        t = torch.full((len(x),), step, dtype=torch.long, device=x.device)
        noise = torch.randn(x.shape, generator=generator, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device) if eta else torch.zeros_like(x)
        x = ddim_step(x, eps_model(x, t), ab[step], previous, eta, noise)
        if return_traj:
            trajectory.append(x.clone())
    return (x, torch.stack(trajectory)) if return_traj else x

@torch.no_grad()
def ddim_invert(eps_model: Callable[[Tensor, Tensor], Tensor], x0: Tensor, alpha_bars: Tensor, num_steps: int) -> Tensor:
    """First-order deterministic inversion; evaluate eps at the current time.

    Returns:
        Return the inverted noisy endpoint Tensor with x0 shape [B,...] and dtype/device, at
        the selected schedule maximum index T-1. Return only the endpoint, not a trajectory.
        Leave x0 unchanged; the output is gradient-free. Discrete inversion is approximate,
        not a promise of bitwise sampling reversibility.
    """
    steps = ddim_timesteps(len(alpha_bars), num_steps).flip(0).tolist()
    ab = alpha_bars.to(x0)
    x = x0.clone()
    current_ab = torch.ones_like(ab[0])
    current_step = 0
    for step in steps:
        t = torch.full((len(x),), current_step, dtype=torch.long, device=x.device)
        eps = eps_model(x, t)
        clean = (x - (1 - current_ab).sqrt() * eps) / current_ab.sqrt()
        x = ab[step].sqrt() * clean + (1 - ab[step]).sqrt() * eps
        current_ab, current_step = ab[step], step
    return x

        and model evaluations use left endpoints t<1.
    """
    if num_steps < 1:
        raise ValueError("num_steps must be positive")
    x = x0.clone()
    trajectory = [x.clone()] if return_traj else None

        x = x + model(x, t) / num_steps
        if return_traj:
            trajectory.append(x.clone())
    return (x, torch.stack(trajectory)) if return_traj else x

import torch
from torch import Tensor


def adamw_step(parameter: Tensor, gradient: Tensor, first_moment: Tensor,
               second_moment: Tensor, step: int, lr: float = 1e-3,
               betas: tuple[float, float] = (0.9, 0.999), eps: float = 1e-8,
               weight_decay: float = 0.01) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Required: return new parameter, first moment and second moment.
    Same-shaped floating tensors; moments start at zero and step starts at 1.
    Apply bias correction, eps outside sqrt, and decoupled decay lr*weight_decay.
    Do not change inputs or add weight decay to gradient/moment estimates.
    Keep tensor autograd paths; the caller decides when to disable gradients.

        as a Python tuple of three floating tensors with the inputs' full

        for the next call, not bias-corrected moments. This is a functional update: return
        new values and leave parameter, gradient and both input moments unchanged. Retain
        tensor autograd paths; the caller decides whether to disable gradients. Do not
        return None as an in-place optimizer step would.
    """

problems.starter:
import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def online_softmax_update(scores: Tensor, values: Tensor, row_max: Tensor,
                          normalizer: Tensor, numerator: Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Required: merge finite scores [Q,K] and values [K,Dv] into online state.
    row_max [Q] starts at -inf, normalizer [Q] and numerator [Q,Dv] at zero.
    Rescale old mass AND weighted values whenever the row maximum changes.
    Return new maximum, unnormalized sum, unnormalized weighted sum.
    Preserve autograd and inputs. All blocks have at least one key.

    Returns:
        Return `(new_max, new_normalizer, new_numerator)` in exactly this order, as a Python
        tuple of floating tensors shaped `[Q]`, `[Q]`, `[Q,Dv]`. Q is the number of query
        rows and Dv the value width. These are the updated row maximum, unnormalized
        exponential mass and unnormalized weighted-value sum over all processed key blocks;
        the numerator is not yet the normalized attention output. Preserve dtype/device,
        autograd and all input state tensors; return updated state rather than updating in
        place.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError()


def block_attention(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, block_size: int = 16) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Provided: tile traversal, no dropout/masks; returns output and per-row log-sum-exp.

    Returns:
        Return `(output, logsumexp)`, a Python tuple of floating tensors `[Q,Dv]` and `[Q]`.
        Q is total query length and Dv value width. output is normalized attention;
        logsumexp is one natural-log sum-exp of scaled scores over all keys per query, not
        an attention-weight matrix. Preserve q/k/v dtype/device and their gradient paths,
        including gradients from logsumexp. Inputs remain unchanged.
    """
    outputs, logsumexp = [], []
    for query_start in range(0, q.shape[0], block_size):
        queries = q[query_start:query_start + block_size]
        row_max = q.new_full((len(queries),), -torch.inf)
        normalizer = q.new_zeros(len(queries))
        numerator = q.new_zeros((len(queries), v.shape[-1]))
        for key_start in range(0, k.shape[0], block_size):
            scores = (queries @ k[key_start:key_start + block_size].T) / math.sqrt(q.shape[-1])
            values = v[key_start:key_start + block_size]
            row_max, normalizer, numerator = online_softmax_update(scores, values, row_max, normalizer, numerator)
        outputs.append(numerator / normalizer[:, None])
        logsumexp.append(row_max + normalizer.log())
    return torch.cat(outputs), torch.cat(logsumexp)

problems.starter:
import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def attention_kernel(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor,
                     mask: Tensor | None = None) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Provided: [B,H,Q,D] attention; True means visible, empty rows are zero.

    Returns:
        Return `(output, weights)` as floating tensors `[B,H,Q,Dv]` and `[B,H,Q,K]`: B batch
        size, H heads, Q/K query/key lengths and Dv value width. Weights sum to one over
        visible keys; a fully masked row has zero output and weights. Preserve the input
        dtype/device and q/k/v autograd with finite gradients for masked rows. This helper
        returns per-head values before concatenation/output projection and does not mutate
        inputs.
    """
    scores = (q @ k.transpose(-1, -2)) / math.sqrt(q.shape[-1])
    if mask is None:
        weights = scores.softmax(-1)
    else:
        allowed = torch.broadcast_to(mask, scores.shape)
        scores = scores.masked_fill(~allowed, -torch.inf)
        scores = torch.where(allowed.any(-1, keepdim=True), scores, torch.zeros_like(scores))
        weights = scores.softmax(-1).masked_fill(~allowed, 0.)
    return weights @ v, weights


def multi_head_attention(query: Tensor, key: Tensor, value: Tensor,
                         w_q: Tensor, w_k: Tensor, w_v: Tensor, w_o: Tensor,
                         num_heads: int, mask: Tensor | None = None) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Required: project, split heads, attend, concatenate, and output-project.
    query [B,Q,D], key/value [B,K,D], all projection matrices [D,D].
    Matrix convention is x @ w (paper layout, not nn.Linear.weight layout).
    D is divisible by num_heads. Boolean mask broadcasts to [B,H,Q,K],
    True means visible. Return output [B,Q,D] and weights [B,H,Q,K].
    Preserve autograd, dtype and device; no bias/dropout; fully masked rows zero.
    The attention kernel above is supplied and may be used unchanged.

    Returns:
        Return `(output, weights)` in that order: floating tensors `[B,Q,D]` and
        `[B,H,Q,K]`, where B is batch size, Q/K query/key lengths, D model width and
        H=num_heads. output has already concatenated heads and applied w_o; weights retain
        each head rather than averaging heads. Preserve input dtype/device and gradients to
        query/key/value and all four projection matrices. Fully masked query rows are zero;
        do not mutate inputs.
    """

module.goal: 在量化前向保持码本值，同时通过冻结的旋转与缩放传递梯度。

problems.starter:
import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def _validate(e: Tensor, q: Tensor, eps: float):
    """Provided input validation.

    Returns:
        Provided helper: return (e_norm, q_norm), two floating Tensors of shape [...,1],
        reducing only the final D features of e/q [...,D] and retaining the dimension. Preserve
        dtype/device and their norm gradient paths; do not mutate inputs. Raise ValueError for
        invalid shape/epsilon, near-zero norms or antiparallel pairs. This returns norms, not
        None.
    """
    if e.shape != q.shape or e.ndim < 1 or e.shape[-1] < 2 or e.numel() == 0:
        raise ValueError("e and q must have equal nonempty [..., D] shapes with D >= 2")
    if not math.isfinite(eps) or eps <= 0:
        raise ValueError("eps must be finite and positive")
    en, qn = e.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True), q.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
    if (en <= eps).any() or (qn <= eps).any():
        raise ValueError("zero or near-zero vectors are outside this exercise")
    if ((e/en + q/qn).norm(dim=-1) <= eps).any():
        raise ValueError("antiparallel pairs do not define this rotation")
    return en, qn


def rotation_quantize(e: Tensor, q: Tensor, eps: float = 1e-8) -> Tensor:
    """Forward q; backward a frozen norm-scaled rotation applied to e.

    Returns:
        Return one floating Tensor with the same [...,D] shape, dtype and device as e and q
        (D>=2); its forward values equal q. Keep the surrogate gradient to e through the frozen
        scaled rotation, but no gradient to q or the rotation/scale construction. Do not detach
        the output, return Jacobians or mutate either input.
    """
    en, qn = _validate(e, q, eps)
    raise NotImplementedError("Freeze the rotation and norm ratio, then transform e")

problems.starter:
import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def _coefficient(value):
    """Provided helper.

    Returns:
        Return None after checking that the Python coefficient is finite and in [0,1]. Raise
        ValueError on failure; no normalized coefficient or Tensor is returned.
    """
    if not math.isfinite(value) or not 0 <= value <= 1:
        raise ValueError("coefficients must be in [0, 1]")


def _log_pair(teacher_logits, student_logits, alpha):
    """Provided helper.

    Returns:
        Return `(teacher_log_probs, student_log_probs)`, a Python tuple of floating tensors
        with the same `[...,V]` shapes/dtype/device as the paired logits; V is vocabulary
        size. These are log probabilities, with no vocabulary reduction. Teacher values are
        detached; student values retain autograd. Validate alpha and equal nonempty
        vocabulary layouts without changing inputs.
    """
    _coefficient(alpha)
    if teacher_logits.shape != student_logits.shape or teacher_logits.ndim < 1:
        raise ValueError("teacher/student logits must have equal nonempty vocabulary shapes")
    if teacher_logits.shape[-1] == 0:
        raise ValueError("vocabulary must not be empty")
    return teacher_logits.detach().log_softmax(-1), student_logits.log_softmax(-1)


def _log_mix(log_a, log_b, alpha):
    """Provided helper.

    Returns:
        Return one floating Tensor with the input log-probability shape `[...,V]`,
        containing the log of the alpha-weighted probability mixture (alpha for log_a,
        1-alpha for log_b). Preserve dtype/device and existing gradient paths; the helper
        does not independently detach either input. Endpoint alpha=0 returns log_b; alpha=1
        returns log_a with a retained zero-gradient path to log_b. Inputs are not modified.
    """
    if alpha == 0:
        return log_b
    if alpha == 1:
        return log_a + log_b * 0.0
    return torch.logaddexp(log_a + math.log(alpha), log_b + math.log1p(-alpha))


def skew_kl(teacher_logits: Tensor, student_logits: Tensor, alpha: float) -> Tensor:
    """Per-position SKL(p || alpha*p + (1-alpha)*q), freezing the teacher.

    Returns:
        Return one floating Tensor shaped `[...]` from logits `[...,V]`, where V is
        vocabulary size and every leading position/batch axis is retained. Each entry is the
        vocabulary-summed skew forward KL at that position; do not average positions.
        Preserve logits' dtype/device and student gradients while freezing teacher logits.
        alpha=1 gives zero with a valid zero student gradient; do not mutate inputs.
    """
    lp, lq = _log_pair(teacher_logits, student_logits, alpha)
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement skew_kl")


def skew_reverse_kl(teacher_logits: Tensor, student_logits: Tensor, alpha: float) -> Tensor:
    """Per-position SRKL(q || (1-alpha)*p + alpha*q), freezing the teacher.

    Returns:
        Return one floating Tensor `[...]` for logits `[...,V]`: V is vocabulary size, and
        leading position/batch axes are unchanged. Each entry is the vocabulary-summed skew
        reverse KL; there is no position or batch reduction. Preserve dtype/device and
        student gradients, freeze teacher logits and leave inputs unchanged. alpha=1 returns
        zero with a valid zero student gradient.
    """
    lp, lq = _log_pair(teacher_logits, student_logits, alpha)
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement skew_reverse_kl")


def distillm2_loss(teacher_t: Tensor, student_t: Tensor, mask_t: Tensor,
                  teacher_s: Tensor, student_s: Tensor, mask_s: Tensor,
                  alpha_t: float = 0.1, alpha_s: float = 0.1,
                  beta: float = 0.5) -> Tensor:
    """Eq. 2 reduction: sum response-token divergences, divide by 2*batch.

    Returns:
        Return one zero-dimensional floating Tensor (`shape == ()`), not a Python number.
        Sum masked token divergences for each source, weight the teacher-response sum by
        1-beta and student-response sum by beta, then divide by 2B (B is the shared batch
        size); do not divide by token count. Empty/all-masked sources contribute zero.
        Preserve the shared floating dtype/device and gradients to both student branches
        only; teacher branches are frozen and masked positions have zero gradients. Inputs
        remain unchanged.
    """
    _coefficient(beta)
    for teacher, student, mask in ((teacher_t, student_t, mask_t), (teacher_s, student_s, mask_s)):
        if teacher.ndim != 3 or teacher.shape != student.shape or mask.shape != teacher.shape[:-1]:
            raise ValueError("expected paired [B,T,V] logits and [B,T] masks")
        if mask.dtype != torch.bool or teacher.shape[0] == 0:
            raise ValueError("masks must be boolean and batch must be nonempty")
    if teacher_t.shape[0] != teacher_s.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("teacher and student response batches must be paired")
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement distillm2_loss")

module.goal: 实现平滑、截断 SVD 和低精度残差双分支前向。
module.goal_en: Implement smoothing, truncated SVD and a quantized residual two-branch forward.
module.scope: 给定平滑系数及 INT fake quantizer；单次 SVD，无校准搜索、FP4、迭代细化或 GPU 内核。
module.scope_en: Given smoothing factors and an INT fake quantizer; one SVD, no calibration search, FP4, iterative refinement or GPU kernels.

problems.starter:
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def fake_quantize(x: Tensor, bits: int = 4) -> Tensor:
    """Provided per-tensor symmetric INT fake quantizer, round ties to even.

    Returns:
        Return one floating Tensor with x's shape/dtype/device: quantized-and-dequantized
        values from the per-tensor symmetric INT grid, not integer codes or a (codes,scale)
        tuple. An all-zero input returns zeros. Inputs are unchanged; gradients through this
        provided rounding helper are not part of the exercise.
    """
    if type(bits) is not int or not 2 <= bits <= 8:
        raise ValueError("bits must be an integer from 2 to 8")
    qmax = 2 ** (bits - 1) - 1
    scale = x.abs().amax() / qmax
    scale = torch.where(scale == 0, torch.ones_like(scale), scale)
    return torch.round(x / scale).clamp(-qmax, qmax) * scale


def _check_smoothing(x, weight, scale):
    """Provided helper.

    Returns:
        Return None after validating nonempty x[B,M], weight[M,N] and positive finite
        scale[M] with matching input-channel sizes. Checked invalid layouts/scales raise
        ValueError. No tensors are changed or returned.
    """
    if x.ndim != 2 or weight.ndim != 2 or scale.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError("expected x[B,M], weight[M,N], scale[M]")
    if x.shape[1] != weight.shape[0] or scale.shape[0] != weight.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError("input channel dimensions must match")
    if min(*x.shape, *weight.shape) < 1 or not torch.isfinite(scale).all() or (scale <= 0).any():
        raise ValueError("nonempty dimensions and finite positive scale required")


def _check_rank(weight, rank):
    """Provided helper.

    Returns:
        Return None when weight is a matrix and rank is a Python int in
        [0,min(weight.shape)]. Invalid rank/layout raises ValueError; no factorization is
        returned and inputs are unchanged.
    """
    if weight.ndim != 2 or type(rank) is not int or not 0 <= rank <= min(weight.shape):
        raise ValueError("rank must be an integer from 0 to min(M,N)")


def smooth_inputs(x: Tensor, weight: Tensor, scale: Tensor) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Preserve XW by dividing X channels and multiplying W rows.

    Returns:
        Return `(xs, ws)`, a Python tuple of floating tensors `[B,M]` and `[M,N]` in the
        same order as x and weight. B is batch size, M input channels and N output channels;
        the smoothed pair satisfies xs@ws=x@weight. Preserve shared dtype/device and leave
        inputs unchanged. This exercise requires inference values, not gradients through the
        quantization pipeline.
    """
    _check_smoothing(x, weight, scale)
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement smooth_inputs")


def split_weight(weight: Tensor, rank: int) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Return truncated-SVD factors L1[M,r], L2[r,N], and unquantized residual.

    Returns:
        Return `(left, right, residual)` as floating tensors `[M,r]`, `[r,N]`, `[M,N]`,
        where weight is `[M,N]` and r=rank. left@right is a best rank-r approximation and
        residual=weight-left@right. Equivalent factor signs/bases are accepted; do not
        return singular values in place of residual. rank=0 gives empty factors and the full
        weight as residual; full rank gives a numerically zero residual. Preserve
        dtype/device without modifying weight; SVD gradients are outside scope.
    """
    _check_rank(weight, rank)
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement split_weight")


def svdquant_linear(x: Tensor, weight: Tensor, scale: Tensor, rank: int,
                    bits: int = 4) -> Tensor:
    """High-precision low-rank branch plus fake-quantized activations/residual.

    Returns:
        Return one floating Tensor `[B,N]`, where x is `[B,M]`, weight is `[M,N]`, B is
        batch size and M/N are input/output channels. This is the combined high-precision
        low-rank and fake-quantized residual output, not a tuple of branches. Preserve
        shared dtype/device and input values; full rank recovers x@weight up to numerical
        error. This is an inference contract with no gradient requirement through
        SVD/rounding.
    """
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement svdquant_linear")

module.goal: 通过加权 L1 折点与深度锚点，精确求解相机坐标点图的尺度及 z 平移。
module.goal_en: Solve shared scale and z translation exactly using weighted L1 breakpoints and depth anchors.
module.scope: 实现 ROE 的全局对齐核心；CPU 小点集枚举，不包含点图网络、多尺度球域或相机恢复。
module.scope_en: Implement the global ROE alignment core on tiny point sets; exclude the point-map network, multi-scale spheres and camera recovery.

problems.starter:
"""Tiny exact ROE solver; enumerate breakpoints instead of production sorting kernels."""
import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def _check_vectors(x, y, weight, trunc):
    """Provided input validation.

    Returns:
        Provided validator: return Python None when x, y and nonnegative weight are finite,
        nonempty, matching 1D floating tensors and trunc is None or finite positive. Raise
        ValueError when a checked condition fails; do not mutate inputs or return transformed
        tensors.
    """
    if x.ndim != 1 or x.numel() == 0 or y.shape != x.shape or weight.shape != x.shape:
        raise ValueError("expected nonempty equal-shaped vectors")
    if not all(t.is_floating_point() and torch.isfinite(t).all() for t in (x, y, weight)):
        raise ValueError("inputs must be finite floating tensors")
    if any(t.dtype != x.dtype or t.device != x.device for t in (y, weight)) or (weight < 0).any():
        raise ValueError("matching dtype/device and nonnegative weights required")
    if trunc is not None and (not math.isfinite(trunc) or trunc <= 0):
        raise ValueError("trunc must be None or finite positive")


@torch.no_grad()
def optimal_scale_1d(x: Tensor, y: Tensor, weight: Tensor,
                     trunc: float | None = None) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Minimize sum min(weight * abs(scale*x-y), trunc); return scale and loss.

    Returns:
        Return the Python tuple (scale, loss) in that order; both are detached scalar floating
        Tensors with shape () and x's dtype/device. loss is the sum of weighted absolute
        residuals, individually capped when trunc is set, not a mean. Ties choose the smallest
        active scale; with no active coefficient return scale zero and its objective. Do not
        mutate inputs.
    """
    _check_vectors(x, y, weight, trunc)
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement the paper core")


def _check_points(prediction, target, mask, trunc):
    """Provided input validation.

    Returns:
        Provided helper: return (valid_prediction, valid_target), floating Tensors [M,3] in the
        original mask-selected order, where M is the number of True mask entries. Preserve point
        dtype/device and leave originals unchanged. Validate nonempty selection and positive
        valid target depths, raising ValueError on checked invalid inputs; masked-out NaNs are
        excluded before value validation. The helper does not itself detach; the solver callers
        are no_grad.
    """
    if prediction.ndim != 2 or prediction.shape[1] != 3 or target.shape != prediction.shape:
        raise ValueError("point maps must be (N, 3)")
    if mask.dtype != torch.bool or mask.shape != prediction.shape[:1] or not mask.any():
        raise ValueError("mask must select at least one point")
    if mask.device != prediction.device:
        raise ValueError("mask device must match")
    p, q = prediction[mask], target[mask]
    _check_vectors(p.flatten(), q.flatten(), torch.ones_like(p).flatten(), trunc)
    if (q[:, 2] <= 0).any():
        raise ValueError("valid target depths must be positive")
    return p, q


@torch.no_grad()
def roe_align(prediction: Tensor, target: Tensor, mask: Tensor,
              trunc: float | None = None) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Exact inverse-depth-weighted L1 alignment with a shared scale and z-only shift.

    Returns:
        Return the Python tuple (scale, z_shift), two detached scalar floating Tensors of shape
        () with the point-map dtype/device. z_shift is a scalar translation only along z, not a
        3-vector; the second return is not an objective value. Fit only masked-valid points; no
        input mutation or solver gradient is required.
    """
    p, q = _check_points(prediction, target, mask, trunc)
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement the paper core")

module.scope: 实现线性观测下的 DAPS Eq.(7) 内核和重加噪。ODE 输出、噪声、循环由脚手架提供；不训练扩散网络。

problems.starter:
"""DAPS Eq. (7), specialized to a supplied linear measurement operator."""
import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def _positive(value, name, allow_zero=False):
    """Provided helper.

    Returns:
        Provided: return Python None when the scalar is valid, not a boolean or a validated
        tensor. Invalid inputs raise ValueError. Validation only: leave inputs and their
        gradient settings unchanged. No returned tensor shape or dtype/device applies.
    """
    if not math.isfinite(value) or value < 0 or (not allow_zero and value == 0):
        raise ValueError(f"{name} has an invalid value")


def _matching(x, *others):
    """Provided helper.

    Returns:
        Provided: return Python None when floating tensors have finite values and matching
        shape/dtype/device, not a boolean or a validated tensor. Invalid inputs raise
        ValueError. Validation only: leave inputs and their gradient settings unchanged. No
        returned tensor shape or dtype/device applies.
    """
    if not x.is_floating_point() or not torch.isfinite(x).all():
        raise ValueError("finite floating tensors required")
    for other in others:
        if other.shape != x.shape or other.dtype != x.dtype or other.device != x.device or not torch.isfinite(other).all():
            raise ValueError("tensor shape/dtype/device must match")


def posterior_score(x: Tensor, x0_hat: Tensor, operator: Tensor, measurement: Tensor,
                    r: float, beta: float) -> Tensor:
    """Score of N(x0_hat, r^2 I) times N(measurement; A x, beta^2 I).

    Returns:
        Return per-sample conditional scores as a Tensor [B, D], matching x shape and
        dtype/device; B counts samples and D unknown coordinates. Measurement width M is not
        an output axis. Do not reduce across samples/coordinates or divide by B or D. Keep
        differentiable tensor operations and leave inputs unchanged.
    """
    _positive(r, "r"); _positive(beta, "beta")
    _matching(x, x0_hat)
    if x.ndim != 2 or operator.ndim != 2 or operator.shape[1] != x.shape[1]:
        raise ValueError("x is (B,D); operator is (M,D)")
    if measurement.shape != (x.shape[0], operator.shape[0]):
        raise ValueError("measurement must be (B,M)")
    for value in (operator, measurement):
        if value.dtype != x.dtype or value.device != x.device or not torch.isfinite(value).all():
            raise ValueError("finite matching dtype/device required")
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement the paper core")


def langevin_step(x: Tensor, score: Tensor, eta: float, noise: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Euler Langevin step; caller supplies fresh standard-normal noise explicitly.

    Returns:
        Return the updated sample Tensor with exactly x shape and dtype/device ([B,D] in
        this exercise, for B samples and D coordinates). Return only the new sample, not the
        score or noise. eta=0 gives x numerically. Do not mutate inputs or explicitly detach
        the output.
    """
    _positive(eta, "eta", allow_zero=True)
    _matching(x, score, noise)
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement the paper core")


def renoise(x0: Tensor, sigma_next: float, noise: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Decoupled transition N(x0, sigma_next^2 I), with fresh independent noise.

    Returns:
        Return one next-level noisy sample Tensor with exactly x0 shape and dtype/device
        ([B,D] here). sigma_next=0 gives x0 numerically. Keep differentiable tensor
        operations and do not mutate x0 or the supplied noise.
    """
    _positive(sigma_next, "sigma_next", allow_zero=True)
    _matching(x0, noise)
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement the paper core")

module.scope: 实现 Eq.(5) 训练核心；提供前向加噪与微型训练脚手架，不包含图像奖励模型、在线采样或 EMA 更新。

problems.starter:
"""DiffusionNFT Eq. (5), with a frozen rollout policy and bounded rewards."""
import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def _check_velocity(current, old, beta):
    """Provided validation helper.

    Returns:
        Provided: return Python None when velocities and beta satisfy the contract, not a
        boolean or a validated tensor. Invalid inputs raise ValueError. Validation only:
        leave inputs and their gradient settings unchanged. No returned tensor shape or
        dtype/device applies.
    """
    if not math.isfinite(beta) or beta <= 0:
        raise ValueError("beta must be finite and positive")
    if current.ndim < 2 or current.numel() == 0 or not current.is_floating_point():
        raise ValueError("velocity needs a nonempty batch and feature dimensions")
    if old.shape != current.shape or old.dtype != current.dtype or old.device != current.device:
        raise ValueError("old and current velocity must match")
    if not torch.isfinite(current).all() or not torch.isfinite(old).all():
        raise ValueError("velocities must be finite")


def implicit_velocities(current: Tensor, old: Tensor, beta: float) -> tuple[Tensor, Tensor]:
    """Return the implicit positive and negative policies; only current receives gradients.

    Returns:
        Return the tuple (positive, negative), in that order. Both are Tensors matching
        current shape [B,...] and dtype/device; B is batch size and trailing axes are
        feature dimensions. Keep both branches differentiable through current, detach old
        inside the function, and leave inputs unchanged.
    """
    _check_velocity(current, old, beta)
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement the paper core")


def nft_loss(current: Tensor, old: Tensor, target: Tensor, rewards: Tensor,
             beta: float) -> Tensor:
    """Mean over examples of reward-weighted squared L2 norms, summed over features.

    Returns:
        Return a scalar Tensor of shape (), with current dtype/device. Sum squared errors
        over all non-batch coordinates within each example, then average over B examples; do
        not average over all elements. Gradients flow only into current; old, target and
        rewards are stopped. Do not mutate inputs.
    """
    _check_velocity(current, old, beta)
    if target.shape != current.shape or target.dtype != current.dtype or target.device != current.device:
        raise ValueError("target velocity must match current")
    if rewards.shape != current.shape[:1] or rewards.dtype != current.dtype or rewards.device != current.device:
        raise ValueError("rewards must be a matching (B,) tensor")
    if not torch.isfinite(target).all() or not torch.isfinite(rewards).all() or ((rewards < 0) | (rewards > 1)).any():
        raise ValueError("finite targets and rewards in [0,1] required")
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement the paper core")

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch import Tensor


def _validate_codes(token_maps, codebook, projections):
    """Provided helper.

    Returns:
        Return a Python `list[int]` of square side lengths, one per token map in input
        order, after validating the scale schedule and tensor layouts. It is not a Tensor.
        Raise ValueError for the checked invalid inputs; do not modify any input.
    """
    if not token_maps or codebook.ndim != 2 or min(codebook.shape) == 0:
        raise ValueError("nonempty token maps and [V,C] codebook required")
    if any(t.ndim != 3 for t in token_maps):
        raise ValueError("token maps must have three dimensions")
    scales = [t.shape[-1] for t in token_maps]
    if scales[0] != 1 or any(a >= b for a, b in zip(scales, scales[1:])):
        raise ValueError("square scales must start at 1 and strictly increase")
    batch = token_maps[0].shape[0]
    for t, n in zip(token_maps, scales):
        if t.ndim != 3 or t.shape != (batch, n, n) or batch == 0 or t.dtype != torch.long:
            raise ValueError("tokens must be nonempty int64 [B,n,n]")
        if t.device != codebook.device or (t < 0).any() or (t >= len(codebook)).any():
            raise ValueError("token indices must be on the codebook device and in range")
    channels = codebook.shape[1]
    if projections.shape != (len(scales), channels, channels):
        raise ValueError("projections must have shape [K,C,C]")
    if projections.dtype != codebook.dtype or projections.device != codebook.device:
        raise ValueError("projection dtype/device must match codebook")
    return scales


def lift_codes(tokens: Tensor, codebook: Tensor, projection: Tensor, full_size: int) -> Tensor:
    """Provided: code lookup, bicubic upsampling, then a fixed channel projection.

    Returns:
        Return one floating Tensor `[B,C,F,F]`, where B is batch size, C the projected
        channel width and F=full_size. It contains codebook features lifted to full spatial
        resolution and channel-projected, in channels-first layout. Preserve the shared
        codebook/projection dtype/device and input values. This helper itself does not
        detach gradients from codebook/projection; next_scale_inputs calls it in a no-grad
        context.
    """
    codes = F.embedding(tokens, codebook).permute(0, 3, 1, 2)
    if codes.shape[-1] != full_size:
        codes = F.interpolate(codes, size=(full_size, full_size), mode="bicubic", align_corners=False)
    return torch.einsum("oc,bchw->bohw", projection, codes)

    Returns:

def next_scale_inputs(token_maps: list[Tensor], codebook: Tensor, projections: Tensor) -> Tensor:

    Returns:

        and L_next=sum(n*n for n in scales[1:]). Concatenate features for target scales 2..K
        in scale order, with row-major spatial tokens within each scale; do not include the
        separate first-scale start embedding. Preserve codebook dtype/device. A single scale

        scales beginning at 1, in-range code indices, codebook [V,C] and matching projections

        output.

def lift_codes(tokens: Tensor, codebook: Tensor, projection: Tensor, full_size: int) -> Tensor:
    """Provided: code lookup, bicubic upsampling, then a fixed channel projection.

    Returns:
        Provided helper: return one floating Tensor [B,C,full_size,full_size] from int64 tokens
        [B,n,n], codebook [V,C] and channel projection [C,C]. Keep the codebook/projection dtype
        and device. The helper itself does not detach differentiable codebook/projection paths;
        the frozen encode/decode callers run under no_grad. No input mutation.

        itself (an alias), not a copy or None. Otherwise return the resized values. Do not
        modify residual in place.

    return F.interpolate(residual, size=(size, size), mode="area") if size != residual.shape[-1] else residual

        Return (token_maps, reconstructions), a Python tuple of two Python lists, each of length

    """

        raise ValueError("features must be nonempty square [B,C,H,H]")

    if features.dtype != codebook.dtype or features.device != codebook.device:
        raise ValueError("feature dtype/device must match codebook")
    _validate_codes([torch.zeros(batch, n, n, dtype=torch.long, device=features.device) for n in scales], codebook, projections)

import math
import torch
from torch import Tensor


def _check_gaussian(mean, covariance):
    """Provided validation helper.

    Returns:
        Provided: return Python None when mean and covariance satisfy the
        Gaussian-statistics contract, not a boolean or a validated tensor. Invalid inputs
        raise ValueError. Validation only: leave inputs and their gradient settings
        unchanged. No returned tensor shape or dtype/device applies.
    """
    if mean.ndim != 1 or mean.numel() < 1 or mean.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.float64):
        raise ValueError("mean must be a nonempty float32/float64 vector")
    if covariance.shape != (mean.numel(), mean.numel()) or covariance.dtype != mean.dtype or covariance.device != mean.device:
        raise ValueError("covariance must be matching (D,D)")
    if not torch.isfinite(mean).all() or not torch.isfinite(covariance).all():
        raise ValueError("Gaussian statistics must be finite")
    tolerance = 50 * torch.finfo(mean.dtype).eps * max(1., covariance.detach().abs().max().item())
    if not torch.allclose(covariance, covariance.T, atol=tolerance, rtol=0):
        raise ValueError("covariance must be symmetric")
    if torch.linalg.eigvalsh(covariance.detach()).min() < -tolerance:
        raise ValueError("covariance must be positive semidefinite")


def _check_pair(mean, covariance, reference_mean, reference_covariance):
    """Provided validation helper.

    Returns:
        Provided: return Python None when generated and reference statistics have matching
        shapes/dtype/device, not a boolean or a validated tensor. Invalid inputs raise
        ValueError. Validation only: leave inputs and their gradient settings unchanged. No
        returned tensor shape or dtype/device applies.
    """
    _check_gaussian(mean, covariance)
    _check_gaussian(reference_mean, reference_covariance)
    if reference_mean.shape != mean.shape or reference_mean.dtype != mean.dtype or reference_mean.device != mean.device:
        raise ValueError("reference and generated statistics must match")


def _check_normalization(distances, weights, eps):
    """Provided validation helper.

    Returns:
        Provided: return Python None when distances, nonnegative weights and positive
        denominators are valid, not a boolean or a validated tensor. Invalid inputs raise
        ValueError. Validation only: leave inputs and their gradient settings unchanged. No
        returned tensor shape or dtype/device applies.
    """
    if distances.ndim != 1 or distances.numel() < 1 or distances.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.float64):
        raise ValueError("distances must be a nonempty float32/float64 vector")
    if weights.shape != distances.shape or weights.dtype != distances.dtype or weights.device != distances.device:
        raise ValueError("weights must match distances")
    if not math.isfinite(eps) or eps <= 0:
        raise ValueError("eps must be finite and positive")
    if not torch.isfinite(distances).all() or not torch.isfinite(weights).all() or (weights < 0).any():
        raise ValueError("distances and nonnegative weights must be finite")
    if (distances <= -eps).any():

                     reference_covariance: Tensor) -> Tensor:

    Returns:

    """
    _check_pair(mean, covariance, reference_mean, reference_covariance)
    raise NotImplementedError("Implement frechet_distance")

import torch
from torch import Tensor

def nucleus_probs(logits: Tensor, p: float, temperature: float = 1.) -> Tensor:
    """Provided: float64 nucleus probabilities in original vocabulary order."""
    # Python floats must not be narrowed to float32 (tiny p/T would become 0).
    work = logits.to(torch.float64)
    if temperature >= 1.:
        scaled = work / temperature
        scaled = scaled - scaled.amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
    else:
        scaled = (work - work.amax(dim=-1, keepdim=True)) / temperature
    probs = torch.softmax(scaled, dim=-1)
    order = torch.argsort(probs, dim=-1, descending=True, stable=True)
    sorted_probs = probs.gather(-1, order)
    previous = torch.cat((torch.zeros_like(sorted_probs[..., :1]), sorted_probs.cumsum(-1)[..., :-1]), dim=-1)
    keep_sorted = torch.ones_like(previous, dtype=torch.bool) if p == 1. else previous < p
    keep = keep_sorted.gather(-1, torch.argsort(order, dim=-1))
    return torch.softmax(scaled.masked_fill(~keep, float('-inf')), dim=-1)

    """Return int64 token IDs [...] from finite CPU logits [..., V].

    generator=generator) once. Choose the first CDF entry strictly above u.
